query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of 5 at.% Re for an equiatomic fraction of Nb in single-phase BCC NbMoTaW (yielding (Nb0.75Re0.05MoTaW) alloy) will (a) raise room-temperature uniaxial tensile ductility from <1 % elongation to ≥5 % without reducing yield strength at 25 °C, (b) maintain <10 % loss of 0.2 % proof strength at 1200–1600 °C relative to the base alloy, and (c) lower irradiation-induced defect density and surface blistering after 2 MeV He²⁺ implantation to 10 dpa at 700 °C by at least 30 % compared with NbMoTaW.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, homogenised (1200 °C/24 h, water-quenched) equiatomic single-phase BCC NbMoTaW alloy with grain size ~50 µm.
generation.intervention: Replace 5 at.% of Nb with rhenium and repeat the identical melt–homogenise route to produce (Nb0.75Re0.05MoTaW) solid-solution alloy, followed by 1000 °C/2 h recrystallisation to obtain comparable grain size.
generation.conditions: Mechanical: tension at 25 °C (quasi-static, 10⁻³ s⁻¹) and high-temperature tests at 1200, 1400, 1600 °C in Ar. Irradiation: 2 MeV He²⁺ to 1 and 10 dpa at 700 °C, vacuum 10⁻⁶ Torr.
generation.structural_mediator: Re atoms segregate to dislocation cores and grain boundaries, reducing local lattice distortion and the Peierls barrier; simultaneous high atomic-mass contrast enhances point-defect recombination and acts as trapping sites for He–vacancy complexes.
generation.mechanism: 1. Solid-solution softening by Re (lowers µ111 and Peierls stress of ½⟨111⟩ screw dislocations) promotes dislocation glide, increasing plastic strain before fracture at 25 °C. 2. Overall solid-solution strengthening from size and modulus mismatch of Re keeps high-T strength essentially unchanged. 3. Chemical/elastic trap distribution provided by Re increases vacancy–interstitial recombination rates and inhibits He bubble coalescence, decreasing swelling and blister formation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated NbMoTaW: • RT uniform elongation rises ≥5× (target ≥5 %). • 0.2 % proof strength at 1200–1600 °C drops ≤10 %. • Post-irradiation TEM shows ≥30 % lower dislocation loop density, bubble number density, and surface blister density.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic NbMoTaW: RT elongation <1 %, 0.2 % proof strength ≈1.2 GPa at 25 °C and ≈450 MPa at 1600 °C; significant loop/bubble population and surface blistering after identical He irradiation.
generation.boundary: Prediction holds for 0–5 at.% Re. Above 8 at.% Re, σ-phase precipitation may occur on slow cooling, degrading high-T strength. Below 600 °C irradiation temperature or >20 dpa, benefits may diminish as Re-mediated defect recombination saturates.
generation.uncertainty: Primary uncertainties: (i) extent of Re segregation achievable without detrimental second-phase formation, (ii) quantitative magnitude of softening vs. strengthening balance, (iii) long-term thermal stability of Re-modified solid solution above 1600 °C.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce NbMoTaW and (Nb0.75Re0.05MoTaW) ingots, homogenise and recrystallise identically. Measure: (1) RT tensile curves; (2) high-T compression at 1200–1600 °C; (3) He²⁺ irradiation at 700 °C to 10 dpa, followed by TEM for loop/bubble density and SEM for blister statistics.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if ANY of the following hold: (a) RT uniform elongation increase <2 % absolute (i.e., <3 % total); (b) high-T (1200–1600 °C average) proof strength drops >10 % relative to baseline; (c) post-irradiation loop or bubble density or blister density not reduced by at least 10 % vs. baseline.
